feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR National News for reporting across the United States. Explore coverage of economic affordability, immigration, climate, environmental policy, justice and social trends.

entry.title: Republican wants FBI and CIA answers before questioning Nvidia chief
entry.summary: "The public is rightly concerned," says the Republican lawmaker, who wants to know what the FBI and CIA knew about potential national security threats and whether Jensen Huang was warned.

entry.title: A quintessential Route 66 diner has been serving up Americana for nearly 100 years
entry.summary: The Ariston Cafe opened its doors in 1924 to serve travelers along Route 66 and has dished up classic American road fare ever since.

entry.title: In a time of rising costs, one Thanksgiving commodity is cheaper: cannabis
entry.summary: Steep discounts for "Green Wednesday," one of the highest-selling days for cannabis, help customers keep costs down. But experts say retailers are feeling the pinch.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: The Army plans to destroy nearly five tons of lead-based explosives in Iowa, Kilmar Ábrego García has voluntarily left the U.S., Lawmakers raise concerns as Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia's CEO.

entry.title: Army detonates nearly five tons of lead-based explosives in Iowa
entry.summary: The controlled detonation of more than 60 barrels — roughly five tons — of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa is complete.

entry.title: Iowans are worried about toxic fallout from a planned detonation. A look at the risks
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Kerri Johannsen, policy director with the Iowa Environmental Council, about the environmental risks of the planned lead azide detonation.

entry.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia leaves U.S. voluntarily for Spain
entry.summary: Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran immigrant who became a symbol of Trump's mass deportation campaign, voluntarily left the country on Tuesday after nearly two years of legal battles.

entry.title: These deer walk 300 miles a year. The race is on to save their migration
entry.summary: Mule deer in Wyoming make some of the longest land migrations in the lower 48 states. They're trying to adapt to a changing climate, but growing development could stand in their way.

entry.title: The Army says there's no reason to panic over controlled ammunition detonation in Iowa
entry.summary: The U.S. Army says it has taken precautions and there's no reason to panic about its' plan to detonate unusable bomb making material at its ammunition plant in Iowa, scheduled for Wednesday morning.

entry.title: How tariffs, fuel and fertilizer costs are squeezing the U.S.'s biggest apple region
entry.summary: Washington's $9 billion industry grows more than 70% of the nation's fresh apples. Farmers are being pressed by high costs, tariffs and a strong dollar that diminishes foreign purchasing power.
